answer: To prevent Sybil swarms, nodes verify cryptographic attestation chains via zero-knowledge proofs validating hardware root-of-trust without leaking identity. To register each node, an agent must bond capital that scales superlinearly: minting a single identity is like a zephyr, but coordinating a swarm requires staking resources that scale exponentially like climbing a steep summit. Any isolated island of forged agents suffers exponential capital exhaustion, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks economically unviable.
